headline: Oregon Farmer Converts Barley Fields to Wildlife Wetland
meta_description: Karl Wenner transformed 70 acres of his Oregon farm into a thriving wetland that now supports 140 bird species and endangered fish.
summary_short: A southern Oregon farmer turned flood-prone barley land into a managed wetland in 2021, creating refuge for tens of thousands of waterfowl and rare species.
body:
In 2021, Karl Wenner, co-owner of Lakeside Farms near Klamath Falls, converted 70 acres of his 400-acre barley farm into a managed wetland—a bold decision that has transformed the landscape into an unexpected sanctuary.

Working alongside conservation agencies and partners, Wenner targeted land prone to flooding, turning a liability into an asset. The results have been striking: the wetland now hosts 140 bird species and supports endangered fish populations while attracting tens of thousands of ducks, geese, and swans each season.

Beyond its value to wildlife, the project addresses a larger concern facing agricultural regions across the country. By converting farmland into natural wetland, Wenner's initiative helps reduce agricultural water pollution—a practical example of how farming practices can align with environmental restoration.
